headline: Chips Lead a Split Tape Into the Weekend; Geopolitical Fog and Key Data Set the Stage
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a fractured note, with semiconductors pulling the tape higher while software stocks absorbed some of the week's heaviest selling. Of the 545 names in our universe, 300 advanced against 242 decliners — a modest but clear edge for the bulls. The semiconductor sector surged 3.05%, propelled by a string of double-digit moves in memory and analog names, while software retreated 1.25% and healthcare shed 0.74%, leaving the broader market's health very much sector-dependent heading into the long weekend.

The standout print of the day came from Sandisk, which rocketed 11.9%, with Semtech, FormFactor, KLA Corp, and Marvell Technology all notching gains above 7%. On the other side of the ledger, Fair Isaac and UiPath each cratered more than 16%, and Autodesk dropped 8.3% — the software complex clearly pricing in a more challenging demand environment. Bloom Energy's 7.35% gain offered a rare bright spot outside of chips.

Looking into the week ahead, traders will navigate a dense geopolitical backdrop, including escalating Middle East tensions following a U.S. strike on an Iranian tanker and renewed Israel-Hezbollah clashes — alongside the implications of strong jobs data for the rate outlook. Volatility premiums deserve respect here.

briefs.headline: U.S. Strike on Iranian Tanker Heightens Gulf Risk Premium
briefs.body: A U.S. military strike struck an Iranian tanker near Kharg Island, according to reports citing Iran's Tasnim news agency. The incident marks a significant escalation in the Gulf and could weigh on crude shipping routes in the week ahead. Energy markets and defense-adjacent names will be on watch.

briefs.headline: Israel-Hezbollah Clashes Intensify Across Lebanon Border
briefs.body: Israeli forces launched strikes into southern Lebanon after a Hezbollah drone launch, and separately announced they had cleared Hezbollah fighters from tunnel networks beneath a key Lebanese ridge. The dual developments signal a broadening of operations and add to the geopolitical uncertainty investors must price this week.

briefs.headline: Strong Payrolls Print Keeps Rate Debate Alive
briefs.body: Friday's jobs data came in firmly above expectations, complicating the Federal Reserve's calculus heading into the next policy meeting. Bond markets will likely re-price the probability of near-term cuts, and rate-sensitive sectors — including homebuilders, which fell 0.27% on Friday — will bear close watching Monday morning.

briefs.headline: U.S. Sanctions Turkish Bank Over Iran Ties, Widening Pressure Campaign
briefs.body: Washington sanctioned a Turkish bank and two of its subsidiaries as part of a broadening effort to choke off financial channels to Iran. The move follows coordinated allied pressure at the IAEA to refer Iran to the UN Security Council, suggesting a multi-front diplomatic and financial squeeze is accelerating.

briefs.headline: Software Selloff Deepens as Automation and Design Names Collapse
briefs.body: UiPath and Autodesk led software lower Friday, falling 16.6% and 8.3% respectively, with PTC and Snowflake also shedding significant ground. The software sector's 1.25% decline was the worst of any group in the session, raising questions about whether demand signals from recent earnings are forcing a broader re-rating of the group.

briefs.headline: Saudi Arabia Arms Deal Adds Fuel to Defense-Sector Outlook
briefs.body: The U.S. government approved a potential $5 billion sale of extended-range munitions to Saudi Arabia, one of the largest single arms packages announced in recent months. The approval lands against a backdrop of rising regional tensions and is likely to sustain investor interest in defense and aerospace names in the sessions ahead.
